name: Nano-Filament Dispersal Unit NFDU-6 'Threadbare'
description: The NFDU-6 deploys a compressed canister payload of approximately 40,000 monofilament-gauge carbon-nanotube threads, each between 2 and 8 centimeters in length, suspended in a rapidly evaporating aerosol carrier. Upon detonation, the carrier disperses the threads in a roughly spherical cloud 6 meters in diameter that hangs in the air for 8–12 seconds before the threads settle. Any exposed biological tissue moving through the cloud at typical human speed contacts the threads with enough relative velocity to drive them into the skin, where they become embedded. The threads themselves cause only minor immediate irritation — the real effect is on cybernetic systems. Each thread is coated with a piezoelectric polymer that generates a micro-current on flexion, and embedded in sufficient density around a cybernetic joint or implant housing, they create constant low-level signal interference that degrades fine motor control and causes sensory implants to misfire.
specifications: form factor: Cylindrical throw-grenade, 90mm length, 45mm diameter, olive-drab with yellow band deployment radius: 6-meter sphere at standard detonation thread count: Approximately 40,000 per unit thread dimensions: 2–8 cm length, 1–3 nanometer diameter suspension duration: 8–12 seconds before threads settle effect on biological tissue: Minor irritation, mild dermal penetration — not acutely dangerous to unaugmented individuals effect on cybernetics: Signal interference, motor degradation, sensory misfiring — severity scales with augmentation density duration of effect: Until threads are removed medically; self-clearing in 6–18 hours for peripheral implants, up to 72 hours for dense augmentation weight: 0.3 kg
tactical_use: Threadbare is used as an area-denial and force-degradation tool rather than a direct incapacitation weapon. Thrown into a corridor before a breach, it degrades the fine motor performance of every augmented defender who enters the cloud zone — not enough to stop them, but enough to make their aim unreliable and their cybernetic reflexes sluggish. Operators who know they are about to enter a Threadbare-contaminated area sometimes don full-body coverage, but this significantly limits mobility. Medical extraction of threads requires specialized equipment; field removal is ineffective and risks driving threads deeper.
cultural_context: Threadbare is widely regarded as a 'dirty' weapon even by operators who have few ethical objections to other prohibited arms. The extended duration of its effects, the medical complexity of removal, and the fact that it affects anyone augmented who enters the zone — not just combatants — has given it a reputation for indiscriminate cruelty. HELIX BIOSYSTEMS officially denies manufacturing it, attributing existing units to a 'discontinued experimental program.' Street-level operators who carry Threadbare are often assumed to be working for employers with no interest in clean operations or civilian collateral.
known_users: Criminal organizations conducting corporate facility raids
Black market arms dealers as demonstration product
A mercenary crew known only as 'The Weavers' who are rumored to use nothing else
story_hooks: A civilian medical clinic in a contested district is treating dozens of patients with Threadbare contamination — someone deployed it in a populated area, and the question of who and why has political implications.

A character with extensive augmentation is contaminated and has 72 hours to find someone with the equipment to remove the threads before a critical job — and the only person with the right tools has their own agenda.
A HELIX BIOSYSTEMS internal document surfaces suggesting the NFDU-6 was not discontinued but is in active production for an undisclosed client.
A Threadbare canister is found at a crime scene that should have been a clean corporate operation — someone is trying to frame a known insurgent group.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian cylindrical grenade with a distinctly medical or industrial aesthetic—more laboratory than battlefield. The form reads as compact and dense, designed for underhand or overhand throw. The yellow warning band wraps around the mid-body like a quarantine marker, immediately signaling hazardous payload.
physical_description.dimensions: 90mm length, 45mm diameter (roughly the size of a AA battery or small lighter)
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively dense and substantial for its compact size—0.3 kg feels weighty in the palm, suggesting a pressurized canister rather than an explosive charge. Balanced, not unwieldy.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade aluminum alloy body with reinforced polymer base cap and impact fuse assembly
physical_description.finish: Matte olive-drab anodized coating—weathered and practical, showing signs of handling. The finish is intentionally non-reflective to avoid detection by visual sensors.
physical_description.color_scheme: Sage olive-drab primary body with a high-visibility yellow warning band (40mm width) centered around the cylinder. Matte black fuse cap with microscopic etching.
physical_description.grip_texture: Smooth anodized aluminum with subtle grip knurling near the base for throwing stability. Non-slip even when wet or bloodied.
distinctive_features: Bright yellow circumferential band with faint HELIX biosecurity warnings printed in small type
Miniature pressure-release valve (brass-colored, 3mm diameter) positioned on the cap for safety venting
Faint micro-etching on the body showing: NFDU-6 | THREADBARE | HELIX BIOSYSTEMS | Batch serial number
Subtle radial cooling fins molded into the base (heat management for piezoelectric payload)
Impact-detonation fuse cap with exposed striker mechanism—designed for hand-throw activation
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: HELIX BIOSYSTEMS logo (stylized double-helix) stamped in metallic ink on the yellow band. Model designation 'NFDU-6' and 'THREADBARE' etched into the lower third. QR code for batch tracking embossed faintly on the opposite side.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field units show consistent wear patterns—micro-scratches from gear contact, slight discoloration on the yellow band from handling oils and grime. Pressure valve may show oxidation if stored in humid environments. Generally appears functional but used, not pristine.
